title: p0395
universal_lens: The structural unification maps economic statics to a zero-curvature phase space where interest vanishes. Productivity acts as the causal Jacobian of organizational transformations, while profit emerges as a topological defect under imperfect competition, quantifying the deviation from equilibrium.
gsi_mapping: GSI models productivity as a conformal kernel estimating causal impact on performance metrics. Interest is treated as a time-decay prior in Bayesian inference, vanishing when predictive distributions achieve stationarity, while profit represents residual variance under competitive constraints.
gse_mapping: GSE treats static conditions as absorbing states in a Markov decision process. Organizational productivity defines transition probabilities between tactical formations. Profit arises as an expected value surplus when state-space symmetry is broken by monopolistic control.

reasoning_traces.think:
The derivation begins by establishing the baseline equilibrium: the static condition. In this zero-curvature limit, the cost of capital over time—interest—must mathematically vanish. This creates a frictionless manifold upon which all economic activity can be projected. From this null-state, we introduce the Causal Productivity Kernel. Unlike classical marginalism, productivity here is not a property of a physical factor, but a geometric property of the organizational transformation itself. It is the Jacobian determinant of the map from input configurations to output realities. When this kernel operates within a perfectly competitive field, returns are driven solely by this causal efficiency. However, the system exhibits a fundamental instability: the Monopoly Tendency Vector. This vector field describes the natural drift of market participants toward positions of structural advantage, creating positive divergence in the distribution of power. As monopoly power concentrates, it distorts the underlying metric of the economic space, generating 'profit' not as a reward for waiting or risk-bearing, but as a toll extracted from the curvature introduced into the market topology. The failure mode occurs when the assumption of perfect mobility breaks down, allowing these monopolistic distortions to become permanent fixtures rather than transient fluctuations.

Consumers and workers react to these rigidifications, creating the friction that manifests as aggregate profit.
